OWN (left): two turrets were built on the LOCAL planet via the real Build-wheel gesture (openBuild funds+docks, KeyW aims the TURRET wedge at 12 o'clock, left-mouse confirms x2, ~10s construction). __healthbarStage.damageTurret(0.4) dropped ONE to 40% hp. VISIBLE: the local planet with its 'YOU' blue ring; a grey turret disc to the planet's right wearing a short BLUE bar (the local player's own colour — the same blue as the YOU ring), partially filled; and a second grey turret disc below the planet at full HP wearing NO bar. The frame was taken in a LULL — bars() = [{owner:0, fraction:0.40, local:false}] was the ONLY drawn bar (the centred ship carries none). So a damaged OWN turret shows an own-colour bar at its rim/orbit position while its full-HP sibling shows nothing. ENEMY (right): a fresh match; the ship flew out into open space (home planet off-frame), then __nameplateStage.stageBot() moved a bot's home planet (Rusty) beside the ship and, with no local turret present, damageTurret(0.35) fell to Rusty's turret. VISIBLE: a grey turret disc wearing a short TEAL bar (Rusty's identity colour), partially filled, with the 'Rusty' nameplate beside it; bars() reported {owner:1, fraction:0.35, local:false}. Threat red is deliberately NOT used on an enemy bar (style-guide S2) — a low enemy turret shows a short bar in ITS owner colour, which is what renders. Together the panels show: damaged own turret (own colour, partial), damaged enemy turret (enemy colour, partial), and a full-HP turret wearing none. No page errors. VERIFIED. title: The "RESPAWNING X…" overlay counts the sim's own clock down — 3, then 1 — then the ship is back and controls returned
attestation: Three frames off a LIVE ?debug=1 match (no ?freeze — the MATCH clock advances 0:15 → 0:17 → 0:18 across the panels, proving the countdown is the running sim, not a still). The local ship was killed with the round-9 write seam window.__planetRush.damageShip(0, 99999); the sim then runs its own respawn clock (RESPAWN_S = 5 s) down and the HUD reads Math.ceil of it (src/ui/respawn-countdown.ts), never a UI-side timer. Each frame is shot off the sim tick counter, and its caption cites the sim-timer value it was taken at. Panel 1 (+150 ticks after death, sim timer ≈ 2.5 s → ceil 3): VISIBLE a "RESPAWNING 3…" pill centred over YOUR home planet in the local player's own blue, with the WAVE 1/5 · Outer Drift / NEXT / MATCH header and the FULL desktop controls strip (WASD Thrust · Mouse Aim · Left mouse Fire/Mine · E Build & Upgrade · Space/Shift Boost · Middle click Ping) present behind it. Panel 2 (+270 ticks, sim timer ≈ 0.5 s → ceil 1): the same overlay now reads "RESPAWNING 1…" — the count has fallen as the clock ran down. Panel 3 (+340 ticks): the ship is BACK at YOUR planet wearing a spawn-protection ring, the overlay is GONE, and the controls strip is returned — the respawn timer elapsed and the sim revived the hull at home. The ceiling numbers on screen (3, then 1) match the sim-timer readback in each caption; death → count-down → return all read legibly. No page errors. VERIFIED.

title: Die, respawn, open the wheel, buy a tier — the tier survives the death and a fresh purchase still lands (DAMAGE ●○○ → ●●○)
attestation: The developer's exact report, off a LIVE ?debug=1 match through the upgrade live-stage seam, with every purchase resolved by the sim's OWN validated buyUpgrade (src/sim/buildings.ts). Sequence: DAMAGE (the WEAPON/power track) bought to tier 1 before dying (buyUpgrade returned {result:'ok', tier:1}); the local ship then KILLED for real via damageShip. Panel 1 (died): VISIBLE the "RESPAWNING" overlay — the ship is genuinely dead on the respawn clock, the state where the sim refuses a purchase 'dead' (its !ship.alive gate, before the docking check). After the sim respawned the hull, the seam read tierOf(power) = 1 — the tier SURVIVED the death. Panel 2 (after respawn, wheel open): VISIBLE the radial upgrade wheel at YOUR planet — hub reads 999 VANGUARD, ENGINE 100%→115%, CARGO 2→4, HULL 50→60 — and the WEAPON wedge reads "DAMAGE ●○○" (one filled pip = the surviving tier 1). Panel 3 (after a fresh post-respawn buy): buyUpgrade returned {result:'ok', tier:2}; VISIBLE the WEAPON wedge now reads "DAMAGE ●●○" (two pips) and the hub ore ticked from 999 down to 991 (8 ore spent). The two zoomed WEAPON-wedge crops beneath isolate the pip moving ●○○ → ●●○. So a tier bought before death survived the respawn intact, and a further tier bought AFTER respawn succeeded with the tier number moving on screen — exactly what the developer asked to see. No page errors. VERIFIED.

title: On an emulated phone, BOOST (button fills, speed ×1.6) and PING (action reaches the sim) both work by touch — no unexplained gap in the parity table's touch column
attestation: An emulated landscape phone (Playwright hasTouch + isMobile, 844×390); every control fired for REAL via CDP touch and read back at the sim through the ?debug=1 input probe (window.__planetRush.input) — which, per docs/input-parity.md, is the sanctioned way to prove the one action (ping) whose effect is not yet rendered. I read docs/input-parity.md and checked its touch column against this build. Panel 1 (affordances): VISIBLE the touch HUD — the left virtual-stick zone plus BUILD & UPGRADE, BOOST, PING and FIRE buttons; the layout registry ids on screen include touch-left-stick, touch-fire-button, touch-boost-button, touch-ping-button and build-button. Every touch verb has a control on screen. Panel 2 (BOOST by touch): holding the BOOST button, VISIBLE the button FILLED and the left stick engaged; the ship's MEASURED top speed rose from 260 to 416 world-units/s — exactly ×1.6, the BOOST_MULTIPLIER (260 is the documented BASE_SPEED) — and the probe read boost.active = true. Panel 3 (PING by touch): a tap on the PING button, VISIBLE the button pressed; the probe latched pingCount 0→1 with a world-space lastPing (1968, 1200) — the ping ACTION crossed into the sim. HONEST LIMIT: the ping MARKER is NOT drawn anywhere on screen — grep of src/render and src/ui finds no ping rendering — which is an EXPLAINED render-side follow-up (input-parity.md §"Known follow-ups: no render-side ping display exists yet"), not a hole in the touch input path; the on-screen tell is therefore the pressed button, not a map pin. Additionally read from touch at the sim this run: thrust (-1, 0) from a left-stick drag and fire.active = true from the FIRE button. Every verb in the parity table's touch column is reachable, the ones I fired (thrust, fire, boost, ping) demonstrably reach the sim, and the single gap — ping visualisation — is documented, so there is NO UNEXPLAINED gap. No page errors. VERIFIED.
